key_insight: SPOD-GPR combines spectral reduced-order modelling with Gaussian process regression to improve parametric predictions and uncertainty calibration over a POD-GPR baseline.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support uncertainty-aware flow prediction for many-query engineering tasks and real-time digital twins.
method: Compress states with parametric POD, then window trajectories and retain their most energetic frequencies.
Apply SPOD at each retained frequency and learn parameter-dependent bases using aligned Grassmann-manifold representations and GPR.
Learn modal coefficients with direct and parameter-conditioned autoregressive GPR, using joint pathwise sampling for predictive uncertainty.
evidence_signal: Across two Kuramoto–Sivashinsky regimes, cylinder flow and elliptic-obstacle flow, tests outside the training parameters and time horizon showed lower normalised mean absolute error and better uncertainty calibration than POD-GPR.
watch_item: Performance beyond the tested extrapolation ranges and computational costs for real-time deployment are not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Parametric spatio-temporal reduced-order modelling via Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and Gaussian Process Regression
